messages:
Connor: Heads-up — seeing a bunch of pods in gpu-pool-us-east stuck in ContainerCreating / failing readiness. ALB health checks are returning 502/timeout for target group. Alerts kicked off ~1712345600.
Mei: Which svc/port is the ALB checking? Any recent infra changes?
Connor: gpu-inference.svc -> NodePort 32080 -> containerPort 8080. kubectl describe shows readiness probe timed out repeatedly.
Connor: ALB logs show health check from 10.10.12.0/22 -> connection timed out. No TCP reset.
Raj: That smells like a network ACL or SG issue. Can someone paste the SG and NACL configs for the subnets that host the worker nodes?
Connor: Quick outputs:
```
# kubectl get pods -n inference
NAME                                READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
gpu-inference-7f9c5d8b6-2k9lm       0/1     ContainerCreating  0          3m

# kubectl describe svc gpu-inference -n inference
Type: NodePort
NodePort: 32080
TargetPort: 8080

# alb health error
2024-04-04T12:34:45Z alb -> 10.0.45.23:32080 connection timed out
```
Mei: Which subnets are the nodes in? public/private? ALB is in public subnets and targets are in private worker subnets right?
Connor: yes: workers in subnet-0a: 10.0.32.0/22 (private), ALB in subnet-1b: 10.0.12.0/22 (public). NAT gateway in public, route tables look fine.
Raj: I'm running a quick NACL check — hold on.
Raj: Found it. The public subnet NACL (subnet-1b) has a DENY rule for ephemeral port range on inbound.
```
# snippet from aws ec2 describe-network-acls
NetworkAclEntries:
 - RuleNumber: 100
   Protocol: -1
   RuleAction: deny
   Egress: false
   CidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
   PortRange: 32768-65535
```
Raj: The NACL is stateless — if inbound ephemeral ports are blocked, return traffic for health checks will get dropped.
Mei: Oof. Any terraform PRs touching that NACL recently?
Connor: PR #842 merged yesterday — it added a deny for high ports to "lock down" public subnets for a compliance req. snippet from the TF change:
```
resource "aws_network_acl_rule" "deny_high_ports" {
  network_acl_id = aws_network_acl.public.id
  rule_number    = 100
  egress         = false
  protocol       = "-1"
  rule_action    = "deny"
  cidr_block     = "0.0.0.0/0"
  port_range {
    from = 32768
    to   = 65535
  }
}
```
Alice: That PR accidentally targeted the public subnet where ALB is. ALB health checks expect to initiate ephemeral connections back to targets. Blocking high ports breaks the TCP handshake.
Connor: Also noticed the worker SG only allows inbound from 10.0.0.0/16 on 32080 but ALB uses its own SG as source, different CIDR (10.0.12.0/22). So two problems: NACL deny + SG source CIDR mismatch.
Mei: Fix plan: (1) remove/relax the NACL deny for ephemeral range for the ALB public subnet OR scope it to only true internet-facing entries, (2) add SG rule to allow ALB SG as source on 32080/8080, (3) verify health checks and pod readiness.
Alice: I'll patch the NACL to allow ephemeral 32768-65535 inbound/outbound for the ALB subnets and add SG rule to worker SG to allow traffic from ALB SG on port 32080.
Connor: Patching now.
Alice: Applied NACL change (allowed ephemeral range) and added SG ingress: source=sg-0ab123 (alb-sg), port=32080, protocol=tcp. Also removed the too-broad deny from TF (creating a hotfix override) and opened a rollback PR.
deploy-bot: Incident update: ingress-policy-hotfix applied by Alice at 1712345688. Monitoring: 3 targets healthy -> 9 targets healthy.
Connor: Confirmed — health checks passed, pods moved to Ready within ~90s. :tada:
Mei: Follow-ups: 1) revert PR #842 or scope it properly, 2) add a CI test that simulates ALB health check from public subnets to private targets (NACL + SG), 3) runbook entry for this class of failure.
Raj: I'll file a postmortem and own the TF fix. Also adding a pre-merge check to warn when NACL denies cover ephemeral ranges in public subnets.
Connor: Thanks everyone. Glad it was NACL+SG and not kernel or kubelet. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Incident resolved — closing alert chain.
